title: Toxic Masculinity & Hyper-Male Mythology in Grappler Baki: Yujiro Hanma, The Dra
summary: Part two of NH's essay on masculinity in Grappler Baki. He reads Yujiro Hanma as the god-like shadow of masculinity, a chaotic hyper-male who forces growth but can never be destroyed. He argues that so-called toxic masculinity is necessary and that tearing it down leaves men and women unprotected.
claims: Labelling parts of masculinity toxic is a modern invention that has dismantled masculine cultural standards and left men fatherless, literally and figuratively
Hero myths, as Campbell describes, both reflect and reinforce masculine identity; male power fantasies keep masculine standards alive across generations
Baki's first arc is a classic monomyth: a boy who must face a god, his father Yujiro, in order to become a man
Yujiro is the shadow of masculinity: no one can beat him because dark masculinity can only be contained for a while, never killed, as in the net-and-tranquilizer scene
Removing the dark side of masculinity entirely would destroy masculine energy as a whole, like pesticide that kills the birds along with the bugs
The answer to toxic masculinity is building virtue through male power fantasies, not deconstruction; positive masculinity builds and exists only because of the threat of destruction
The hyper-male (villain, chaos, instinct) must be distinguished from the alpha male (hero, order, hierarchy); one is masculinity itself, the other its peak
Yujiro is a terrible father because his parenting uses only negative reinforcement, yet shielding a child from all negativity is equally harmful; the father brings challenges, the mother comfort
Toxic masculinity always comes from imbalance, either too little or too much masculinity
Yujiro is like a tyrant who must be killed to be replaced, while an alpha is like a democratic leader who steps down
Manhood is both sword and shield, a cultural answer to the chaos of male biology, and has always been needed
Yujiro killing Baki's mother symbolises the vulnerable dying when masculinity fails to protect them; modern women who attack masculinity weaken their own protection
